units.translation: Will you not speak of anarchy?
You seem to be saying nothing.
Many things—to speak in vain.
But if you have said everything.
You have spoken a true account about the order of things.
It has been said.

But if you can say what remains of the toils, tell me.
These things require a long time to tell.
May you never say that Zeus—
Apollo—having said three times that he would save the city from dying without offspring.
Perhaps someone might say.
It is possible to speak over the wretched.
Alone of mortals he could speak the end.
so to speak a word
And thus he spoke, uttering portents.
And the old lord said this, speaking aloud.
They can speak of the blow of Zeus.
And someone rebuking me said.
She spoke thus.
How then could you, by speaking good and true things, succeed?
I wish to speak once more a speech or a lament.
I will not be ashamed to say the opposite.
What should I say?
How should I speak kindly?
For he spoke, revealing to mortals the soothing offerings from the earth of the hostile-minded.
But what would we achieve by saying (where φάντες [having spoken] has been restored for the sake of the meter)?
Before he himself speaks, what countryman is the stranger?
The man spoke boldly to the man.
Unknown to unknown, the man spoke, having met him.
Having heard such things, I spoke.
What of these things could you say so as to make clear to my mind?
How, by saying what is equal, could I accomplish it?
You might call it a net.
But now a third savior has come from somewhere—or should I say doom?
What do you wish to say in turn to these things, stranger?
But indeed you must say how you killed.
I never spoke in the prophetic seats.
I said that she was such.
So that you may never say that I perish dishonored.
I said before too, that I would not do these things without the people.
May the people never say—honoring newcomers, you destroyed the city.
To what local protectors did you say this?
Saying to the gods that he does not revere the gods.
And to say it is somehow an easy pollution.
And having said everything.
He himself having said these things.
What did you say?
You spoke a great light to my house.
How did you say?
You spoke reasonably because of my absence.
You have spoken heavy words, that a new war be raised.
You said this to him.

But you speak.

Say a lament.
But you speak.
And indeed say this, not against my judgment.
To your parents—say that Orestes is dead.
But speak likewise also of your father's mother.
Say first whether you killed your mother.
